question: A startup is about to launch its mobile app in several new countries. It wants users in each country to get a fast experience without the company building or leasing its own data centers abroad. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud addresses this need?

options.text: Eliminating the need to protect any customer data
Receiving physical access to AWS data centers in every country
Reserving a fixed amount of hardware capacity for several years
Deploying applications in multiple AWS Regions around the world within minutes

explanation: The AWS global infrastructure lets customers deploy applications in multiple Regions quickly, which brings applications closer to users and removes the need to build physical facilities.

optionExplanations.A: Customers remain responsible for protecting their own data under the shared responsibility model.
optionExplanations.B: AWS does not provide customers with physical access to its data centers.
optionExplanations.C: Fixed multi-year capacity is the opposite of the on-demand, elastic model of the cloud.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Going global in minutes is one of the six advantages of cloud computing.

keyConcept: Global reach: deploy in multiple Regions in minutes instead of building data centers.

question: A company wants to stop guessing how much server capacity it will need. Instead, it wants to pay only for the compute it actually consumes and add or remove capacity as demand changes. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud matches this requirement?

options.text: Trade capital expense for variable expense
Receive volume discounts based on a five-year commitment
Get dedicated hardware that is never shared with other customers
Eliminate all networking costs between services

explanation: Trading capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense means you pay only for what you use, eliminating idle capacity and allowing you to scale elastically.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Variable expense and stopping capacity guessing are two of the six advantages of cloud computing.
optionExplanations.B: Volume discounts exist but do not require a five-year commitment; this also does not address on-demand elasticity.
optionExplanations.C: Dedicated hardware (Dedicated Hosts/Instances) is optional; it is not a universal benefit and adds cost.
optionExplanations.D: Networking between services is not free; data transfer costs still apply.

keyConcept: Six cloud advantages: trade CapEx for variable cost, stop guessing capacity, increase speed and agility, go global.

question: An AWS customer benefits from lower per-unit costs because AWS aggregates usage across hundreds of thousands of customers. What is this cloud benefit called?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Trade fixed expense for variable expense

explanation: Because AWS aggregates demand from many customers, it achieves higher economies of scale, which translates into lower pay-as-you-go prices for customers.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Massive economies of scale is one of the six advantages, referring to lower prices driven by aggregated usage.
optionExplanations.B: Speed and agility refers to being able to experiment quickly, not to price reductions from scale.
optionExplanations.C: Eliminating data center costs is also an advantage, but it refers to offloading undifferentiated heavy lifting, not price from scale.
optionExplanations.D: Variable expense relates to the payment model, not the price reduction from pooled usage.

keyConcept: Economies of scale: AWS aggregates usage across many customers, passing lower prices back to you.

question: A company's development team used to wait weeks for IT to provision servers for a new project. After migrating to AWS, the team can spin up compute resources in minutes. Which cloud advantage does this illustrate?

options.text: Stop spending money on running and maintaining data centers
Benefit from massive economies of scale

explanation: Increasing speed and agility means developers can provision resources in minutes rather than weeks, lowering the cost and time of experimentation.

optionExplanations.A: Eliminating data center costs is about not running your own facilities, not about provisioning speed.
optionExplanations.B: Going global refers to deploying in multiple geographic Regions, not to internal provisioning speed.
optionExplanations.C: Economies of scale describe price reductions from pooled demand, not provisioning speed.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Provisioning from weeks to minutes describes increased speed and agility.

keyConcept: Speed and agility: provision resources in minutes, reduce experimentation costs.

question: A company is evaluating a move to AWS. The CFO wants to know which TWO financial benefits moving to the cloud typically provides.

options.text: Converting large upfront capital expenditures to smaller variable operational costs
Permanently fixing infrastructure costs regardless of usage
Benefiting from lower prices through AWS's economies of scale
Receiving a guaranteed 100% SLA across all services

explanation: Moving to the cloud converts CapEx to variable OpEx and lets customers benefit from economies of scale that AWS passes on as lower prices.

optionExplanations.A: Software licensing still applies; BYOL or license-included models vary and are not universally eliminated.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. CapEx to variable OpEx is a core financial benefit of cloud adoption.
optionExplanations.C: Costs vary with usage in the cloud — the opposite of fixed costs.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. AWS passes economies of scale back to customers through lower prices over time.
optionExplanations.E: No service offers a universal 100% SLA; individual SLAs vary by service.

keyConcept: Cloud economics: CapEx → OpEx and economies of scale lower your per-unit costs.

question: Which of the following is an example of the cloud benefit 'stop spending money running and maintaining data centers'?

options.text: Using AWS Lambda so you focus on code instead of managing servers
Using Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances to lower compute costs
Deploying an application in multiple AWS Regions simultaneously
Using CloudWatch alarms to detect when CPU utilization is too high

explanation: Running serverless workloads like AWS Lambda means you do not provision or manage the underlying hardware, letting you focus on code — which exemplifies eliminating data center overhead.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Serverless removes infrastructure management, illustrating the 'stop running data centers' advantage.
optionExplanations.B: Reserved Instances reduce cost but you still manage the EC2 instances.
optionExplanations.C: Multi-Region deployment illustrates going global in minutes, not eliminating data center operations.
optionExplanations.D: CloudWatch alarms monitor resources; they don't eliminate the need to manage the infrastructure.

keyConcept: Undifferentiated heavy lifting: AWS handles hardware/facilities so you focus on your application.

question: A company runs a website that experiences significant traffic spikes during product launches. After each launch, traffic drops back to a baseline. Which cloud characteristic allows the company to automatically handle these spikes without paying for idle capacity the rest of the time?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to acquire and release resources dynamically as demand changes, so the workload handles spikes while not paying for idle capacity during quieter periods.

optionExplanations.A: Fault tolerance refers to the ability to continue operating when a component fails, not to dynamic scaling.
optionExplanations.B: High availability focuses on minimizing downtime, not on dynamically matching capacity to demand.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Elasticity means scaling up during spikes and scaling down when demand drops.
optionExplanations.D: Durability refers to the ability of data storage to retain data without loss, not to compute scaling.

keyConcept: Elasticity: dynamically scale resources up and down to match demand and cost.

question: A company's on-premises infrastructure is underutilized most of the year because it was sized for the annual peak. Which cloud value proposition resolves this problem?

options.text: Purchasing Reserved Instances for the peak capacity
Using AWS Support to predict future capacity needs
Migrating all workloads to a single large Dedicated Host
Moving to a pay-as-you-go model with elasticity

explanation: On-premises environments are typically over-provisioned to handle peak demand. The cloud's pay-as-you-go and elastic model means you pay only for what you need when you need it.

optionExplanations.A: Reserved Instances still pre-commit to a fixed capacity, which does not solve the idle-time cost problem.
optionExplanations.B: Support plans help with guidance but cannot solve the fundamental problem of fixed-capacity pricing.
optionExplanations.C: Dedicated Hosts offer dedicated hardware but still require capacity planning and do not provide elasticity.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. On-demand/elastic pricing eliminates idle over-provisioned capacity.

keyConcept: Stop guessing capacity: the cloud lets you match resources to demand and avoid idle waste.

question: An infrastructure team is responsible for purchasing, racking, stacking, and cabling servers in a corporate data center. After a full cloud migration, which of these tasks is still the team's responsibility?

options.text: Physical security of the server racks
Replacing failed disk drives in the servers
Designing the application architecture and selecting cloud services
Provisioning power and cooling for the facility

explanation: After a cloud migration, AWS owns the physical layer. The customer team shifts focus to architectural decisions — which services to use and how to design the application — rather than hardware.

optionExplanations.A: Physical security of data center facilities is AWS's responsibility after migration.
optionExplanations.B: Hardware maintenance including disk replacements is managed by AWS.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Application design and service selection remain customer responsibilities.
optionExplanations.D: Power and cooling are managed by AWS as part of the facility infrastructure.

keyConcept: Cloud eliminates undifferentiated heavy lifting (hardware), freeing teams for higher-value work.

question: Which TWO pillars are part of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is built on six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Operational Excellence is one of the six Well-Architected pillars.
optionExplanations.B: Cost Accounting is a business finance term, not a Well-Architected pillar (the pillar is Cost Optimization).
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Reliability is one of the six Well-Architected pillars.
optionExplanations.D: Network Virtualization is a networking concept, not a Well-Architected pillar.
optionExplanations.E: Hardware maintenance is managed by AWS, not a Well-Architected pillar.

keyConcept: Cloud provisioning speed: minutes vs. months for on-premises hardware acquisition.

question: A company wants to reduce the amount of time its developers spend on tasks that don't differentiate its product, such as patching operating systems and managing load balancers. Which cloud principle describes this goal?

options.text: Adopt a capital expenditure pricing model
Reduce time on undifferentiated heavy lifting

explanation: AWS aims to reduce undifferentiated heavy lifting — the commodity tasks like hardware provisioning and OS patching that don't give companies a competitive edge — so teams can focus on unique business logic.

optionExplanations.A: The goal is to reduce, not increase, time on undifferentiated heavy lifting.
optionExplanations.B: Capital expenditure (CapEx) is the on-premises model the cloud replaces with OpEx.
optionExplanations.C: The cloud moves away from commodity hardware purchasing to on-demand consumption.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. The cloud lets customers shift time from commodity IT tasks to differentiating work.

keyConcept: Undifferentiated heavy lifting: AWS handles commodity tasks so you focus on what makes your business unique.

question: Which AWS service characteristic enables a customer to use as little as one virtual server or scale to thousands, depending on demand, without any upfront commitment?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to scale resources up or down seamlessly and on demand. AWS Auto Scaling and services like Amazon EC2 allow this without upfront commitments.

optionExplanations.A: Fault tolerance is designing systems to continue operating despite component failures.
optionExplanations.B: Confidentiality is a security property about protecting data from unauthorized access.
optionExplanations.C: Durability relates to data persistence and resistance to data loss, typically in storage services.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Elasticity describes dynamic scaling from minimal to massive capacity on demand.

keyConcept: Elasticity: scale from 1 to thousands of instances on demand, no upfront commitment.

question: A company needs to design its workload so it can recover from infrastructure failures and dynamically acquire resources to meet demand. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar covers this?
explanation: The Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on a workload's ability to perform its intended function correctly and consistently, including recovery from failures and dynamic resource acquisition.

optionExplanations.A: Performance efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements.
optionExplanations.B: Operational excellence focuses on running systems and continually improving processes and procedures.
optionExplanations.C: Cost optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Reliability covers failure recovery and dynamically meeting demand.

keyConcept: Well-Architected Reliability pillar = recover from failures + dynamically acquire resources.

question: A cloud architect team is reviewing cost allocation to ensure they are spending money only on what they actually need. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar guides this review?
explanation: The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs by understanding and controlling where money is being spent.

optionExplanations.A: Sustainability focuses on reducing environmental impact.
optionExplanations.B: Reliability focuses on recovery from failures and meeting demand.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Cost optimization is about spending wisely and avoiding waste.
optionExplanations.D: Security covers protecting data and systems, not spend management.

keyConcept: Cost Optimization pillar: spend only on what you need, identify waste, use savings plans.

question: A company wants to implement a design where if one component fails, the overall application continues to serve users. Which design principle from the AWS Well-Architected Framework Reliability pillar applies?
explanation: The Reliability pillar recommends monitoring key metrics and triggering automation to recover automatically from failure, ensuring minimal user impact.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Automatically recovering from failure is a core Reliability design principle.
optionExplanations.B: Serverless is a technology choice that can help reliability but is not a named Well-Architected design principle.
optionExplanations.C: Implement traceability is a Security pillar design principle for monitoring and auditing.
optionExplanations.D: Enable people to perform actions is an Operational Excellence principle about giving teams the tools they need.

keyConcept: Reliability design principle: automatically recover from failure using monitoring and automation.

question: Which TWO migration strategies are part of the 7 Rs defined by AWS for cloud migration?
explanation: The 7 Rs of cloud migration are Rehost, Replatform, Refactor (Re-architect), Repurchase, Relocate, Retain, and Retire.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Rehost (lift-and-shift) moves applications without code changes.
optionExplanations.B: Replicate is a data synchronization mechanism, not a 7 Rs migration strategy.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Refactor involves redesigning applications for cloud-native features.
optionExplanations.D: Restart is an operational action, not a migration strategy.
optionExplanations.E: Reboot is a system restart, not a migration strategy.

keyConcept: Operational Excellence: make frequent, small, reversible changes to reduce risk.

question: A security team wants to protect data in transit and at rest, and to give team members only the minimum access they need. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar provides design guidance for this?
explanation: The Security pillar covers data protection (in transit and at rest), identity and access management (least privilege), and incident response.

optionExplanations.A: Operational excellence focuses on process and procedure, not data protection or access control.
optionExplanations.B: Reliability focuses on recovery and availability, not access control or encryption.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. The Security pillar addresses least-privilege access, encryption, and data protection.
optionExplanations.D: Sustainability focuses on reducing the environmental footprint of workloads.

keyConcept: Security pillar: least privilege access, encrypt data in transit and at rest.

question: An e-commerce company wants to ensure its application can handle 10× more users than normal during a sale event without reconfiguring the infrastructure manually. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework design principle supports this?

options.text: Use managed services to reduce operational burden
Scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability

explanation: Horizontal scaling adds more small resources rather than replacing one resource with a larger one, increasing capacity for large demand events while maintaining reliability.

optionExplanations.A: Observability is about monitoring and gaining insight, not about scaling to handle demand.
optionExplanations.B: Managed services reduce operational burden but do not specifically describe horizontal scaling for demand spikes.
optionExplanations.C: Technical debt remediation improves maintainability, not immediate capacity handling.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Horizontal scaling (adding more instances) is a Reliability/Performance Efficiency design principle to handle load increases.

keyConcept: Horizontal scaling: add more resources to handle increased load without reconfiguring.

question: A solution architect is reviewing a workload using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. Which TWO pillars focus MOST on the long-term sustainability and ongoing improvement of operations?
explanation: Operational excellence is about continually improving processes and procedures. Sustainability focuses on minimising the environmental impact of workloads. Both are explicitly about long-term improvement and responsibility.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Operational excellence is defined around continuous improvement of operations.
optionExplanations.B: Reliability focuses on workload availability and failure recovery, not ongoing process improvement.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Sustainability is about long-term environmental improvement of cloud workloads.
optionExplanations.D: Performance efficiency is about using resources efficiently, not specifically ongoing process improvement.
optionExplanations.E: Cost optimization reduces waste but is primarily focused on financial efficiency, not operational process improvement.

keyConcept: Operational excellence = continuous process improvement; Sustainability = long-term environmental responsibility.

question: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar would a team consult when choosing between using AWS-managed services versus self-managed software to reduce the amount of patching and infrastructure management required?
explanation: Operational excellence includes using managed services to reduce operational burden as a design principle, because managed services reduce patching, upgrades, and infrastructure management.

optionExplanations.A: Cost optimization can benefit from managed services, but the primary driver described (reducing operational burden) maps to Operational Excellence.
optionExplanations.B: Security focuses on protective controls, not on reducing administrative overhead through service selection.
optionExplanations.C: Performance efficiency focuses on resource efficiency and technology selection for performance, not operational burden reduction.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Operational Excellence's principle of using managed services directly addresses this scenario.

keyConcept: Operational Excellence: use managed services to reduce undifferentiated operational heavy lifting.

question: Which TWO advantages of cloud computing directly relate to financial flexibility and cost management?

options.text: Trade capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense (OpEx)
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Guaranteed zero monthly electricity costs on-premises

explanation: Two major financial advantages of the AWS Cloud are trading capital expenses (CapEx) for variable operational expenses (OpEx) and benefiting from AWS massive economies of scale.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The cloud eliminates upfront infrastructure CapEx in favor of pay-as-you-go OpEx.
optionExplanations.B: Manual hardware installation is an on-premises burden, not a cloud advantage.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. AWS aggregates high usage volume to pass on lower variable costs to customers.
optionExplanations.D: On-premises electricity costs are not eliminated by AWS unless on-premises facilities are decommissioned.
optionExplanations.E: Mandatory upfront fees run counter to cloud variable pricing.

keyConcept: AWS CAF: aligns cloud capabilities to business outcomes across 6 perspectives (Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations).

question: A company is using the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) to guide its cloud migration. Its HR and training teams are involved in building new skills and ensuring employees are ready for cloud roles. Which CAF perspective covers this?
explanation: The People perspective of the AWS CAF focuses on culture, structure, roles, and training — ensuring that the organisation and its workforce are ready for cloud adoption.

optionExplanations.A: The Business perspective aligns IT investments with business strategy and identifies value drivers.
optionExplanations.B: The Platform perspective focuses on cloud infrastructure, architecture, and technology decisions.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. The People perspective addresses organizational readiness, training, and cultural change.
optionExplanations.D: The Operations perspective addresses monitoring, incident management, and day-to-day cloud operations.

keyConcept: AWS CAF People perspective: organizational readiness, roles, training, and culture.

question: A company completes its cloud migration. One of the stated benefits is that experimenting with new ideas costs less because failed experiments can be terminated quickly and resources released. Which migration benefit does this illustrate?

options.text: Guaranteed cost savings compared with on-premises
Elimination of all software licensing costs

explanation: The cloud's on-demand model means experiments are cheap: spin up, test, and shut down quickly. This reduces the cost of failure and accelerates innovation, a key migration benefit.

optionExplanations.A: Security posture can improve, but the scenario specifically describes innovation and experimentation speed.
optionExplanations.B: Cost savings depend on workload type and usage patterns; they are not guaranteed for all scenarios.
optionExplanations.C: Licensing costs vary; not all are eliminated by moving to the cloud.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Low-cost experimentation and fast iteration are core innovation and agility benefits of cloud migration.

keyConcept: Cloud enables low-cost experimentation: start, test, shut down quickly without stranded capital.

question: Which cloud migration strategy involves moving an application to the cloud without modifying it at all, essentially re-hosting it on cloud infrastructure?
explanation: Rehosting (lift and shift) moves an application to the cloud without code changes. The application runs on cloud infrastructure but the architecture stays the same.

optionExplanations.A: Refactoring re-architects the application significantly to take full advantage of cloud-native features.
optionExplanations.B: Replatforming makes minimal optimizations (e.g., moving to a managed database) without full code refactoring.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Rehosting = lift and shift: move as-is to cloud infrastructure without modification.
optionExplanations.D: Retain means keeping the application on-premises or deferring migration.

keyConcept: Migration 7 Rs: Rehost (lift and shift) = move to cloud without code changes.

question: A company is considering migrating to AWS. Which TWO outcomes can the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) help the company achieve?

options.text: Increased revenue opportunities through digital innovation
Automatic elimination of all compliance obligations
Permanent reduction in all IT staff headcount

explanation: The AWS CAF is designed to help organisations achieve business outcomes including reduced risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue, and increased operational efficiency.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Reduced business risk is one of the four AWS CAF business outcomes.
optionExplanations.B: The CAF does not guarantee zero-downtime migration; that depends on architecture and planning.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Increased revenue through digital innovation is a key AWS CAF outcome.
optionExplanations.D: Compliance obligations remain and must be addressed within the cloud; the CAF does not eliminate them.
optionExplanations.E: The CAF addresses workforce evolution, not headcount elimination.

keyConcept: AWS CAF outcomes: reduced risk, ESG improvement, revenue growth, operational efficiency.

question: A company's migration team is assessing which of its 200 applications should be migrated to AWS first, which should be refactored, and which should be retired. Which migration strategy is described by 'retiring' an application?

options.text: Rehosting it on Amazon EC2 as-is
Re-architecting it as a microservices application
Moving it to a SaaS application
Decommissioning it because it is no longer needed

explanation: In the migration 7 Rs framework, 'Retire' means decommissioning applications that are no longer needed. This reduces the portfolio size and can eliminate maintenance costs.

optionExplanations.A: Rehosting is lift and shift to cloud infrastructure without changes.
optionExplanations.B: Re-architecting as microservices is the 'Refactor/Re-architect' strategy.
optionExplanations.C: Replacing with a SaaS product is the 'Repurchase' strategy.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Retire = decommission applications that have been identified as no longer providing business value.

keyConcept: Migration Retire: decommission applications that are no longer needed to reduce portfolio and cost.

question: A company has a legacy monolithic application that it wants to rewrite as cloud-native microservices to take full advantage of AWS services. Which migration strategy applies?
explanation: Refactoring (re-architecting) involves rethinking the application architecture and rewriting it to leverage cloud-native capabilities such as microservices, containers, and serverless.

optionExplanations.A: Rehosting moves the application as-is without modification.
optionExplanations.B: Replatforming makes minor adjustments (e.g., managed database) but does not involve a full rewrite.
optionExplanations.C: Retain keeps the application in its current environment.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Refactor/Re-architect involves redesigning and rewriting the application to use cloud-native services.

keyConcept: Refactor: redesign and rewrite the application to be cloud-native (microservices, serverless, containers).

question: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) perspective addresses the risk, compliance, and audit requirements an organisation must manage during cloud adoption?
explanation: The Governance perspective of the AWS CAF identifies capabilities needed to manage risk, ensure compliance, and optimise cloud expenditure across the organisation.

optionExplanations.A: The Business perspective aligns IT and business strategy and value drivers.
optionExplanations.B: Security focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets on the cloud.
optionExplanations.C: Operations focuses on managing and running cloud services day to day.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Governance covers risk management, compliance, portfolio management, and financial oversight.

keyConcept: AWS CAF Governance perspective: risk management, compliance, portfolio management.

question: A company notices that many of its Amazon EC2 instances use only a small fraction of their CPU and memory. The company wants to lower costs by matching instance types and sizes to the actual workload needs. Which practice does this describe?
explanation: Rightsizing means matching instance types and sizes to workload performance and capacity requirements at the lowest possible cost. Tools such as AWS Compute Optimizer provide recommendations.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Rightsizing removes wasted capacity by fitting resources to real usage.
optionExplanations.B: BYOL is a software licensing strategy and does not change instance sizing.
optionExplanations.C: This is not a recognized cost optimization practice for instance sizing.
optionExplanations.D: Multi-Region failover supports resilience and typically adds cost rather than reducing it.

keyConcept: Rightsizing = fit resource size to actual demand to cut waste.

question: A company has predictable, steady-state compute usage and wants to lower its Amazon EC2 costs compared to On-Demand pricing without managing any servers itself. Which EC2 pricing model offers the highest discount for this scenario?

options.text: Reserved Instances or Savings Plans with a 1- or 3-year term

explanation: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans offer significant discounts (up to 72% vs On-Demand) in exchange for a 1- or 3-year usage commitment, making them ideal for steady, predictable workloads.

optionExplanations.A: Spot Instances can be cheaper but can be interrupted, making them unsuitable for steady-state critical workloads.
optionExplanations.B: Dedicated Hosts are more expensive than standard instances; they address compliance/licensing needs.
optionExplanations.C: On-Demand offers no discount and is the baseline pricing.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Committed usage plans (RIs or Savings Plans) offer the biggest discounts for predictable workloads.

keyConcept: Reserved Instances / Savings Plans: up to 72% savings for predictable, committed usage.

question: A company runs batch processing jobs that are fault-tolerant and can be interrupted. The company wants to use EC2 at the lowest possible cost. Which pricing model should it use?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare AWS capacity and can be up to 90% cheaper than On-Demand. They can be interrupted with a two-minute notice, making them ideal for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch jobs.

optionExplanations.A: On-Demand is flexible but more expensive than Spot for non-critical workloads.
optionExplanations.B: Reserved Instances are for steady-state workloads that run continuously, not occasional batch jobs.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Spot Instances are the cheapest option for interruptible, fault-tolerant workloads.
optionExplanations.D: Savings Plans provide discounts for consistent usage; they don't apply to highly variable batch jobs as effectively.

keyConcept: Spot Instances: up to 90% discount, can be interrupted — best for fault-tolerant batch/data processing.

question: Which AWS tool analyzes EC2 instance utilization metrics and provides recommendations to rightsize instances to reduce cost?
explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze resource configurations and utilization metrics, then recommends optimal EC2 instance types, sizes, and other resources to reduce cost and improve performance.

optionExplanations.A: Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes cost and usage data; it doesn't provide instance-level rightsizing recommendations.
optionExplanations.B: AWS Budgets alerts you when spending exceeds thresholds; it doesn't analyze instance utilization.
optionExplanations.C: Trusted Advisor provides checks across cost, security, performance, and reliability, including some rightsizing, but Compute Optimizer is the dedicated rightsizing service.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Compute Optimizer specifically analyzes workload metrics and recommends rightsizing.

keyConcept: AWS Compute Optimizer: ML-based rightsizing recommendations for EC2, Lambda, EBS, and more.

question: A company wants to avoid unexpectedly large AWS bills. It wants to receive an alert when its projected monthly spend exceeds a threshold it sets. Which AWS service provides this capability?
explanation: AWS Budgets lets you set custom cost and usage budgets. You can configure alerts via email or Amazon SNS when actual or forecasted costs exceed your defined thresholds.

optionExplanations.A: Cost Explorer visualizes historical cost data but does not create alerts for future spend.
optionExplanations.B: Compute Optimizer provides resource rightsizing recommendations, not billing alerts.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. AWS Budgets sends alerts when actual or forecasted spend exceeds a defined threshold.
optionExplanations.D: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs for planned architectures; it is not for monitoring live accounts.

keyConcept: AWS Budgets: set thresholds and receive alerts when actual or forecasted spend exceeds limits.

question: A company wants to reduce its AWS spending. Which TWO actions are recommended cost optimization strategies?

options.text: Turn off development and test environments when they are not in use
Run all workloads on the largest EC2 instance type available to avoid running out of resources
Purchase Savings Plans for predictable workloads
Enable full access to all AWS services for all employees to maximize flexibility
Store all data indefinitely in Amazon S3 Standard without lifecycle policies

explanation: Turning off unused environments and purchasing Savings Plans for predictable workloads are both standard cost optimization practices. The others increase cost or risk.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Stopping non-production environments when idle eliminates unnecessary compute spend.
optionExplanations.B: Oversizing wastes money; rightsizing to match actual needs is the best practice.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Savings Plans lock in discounts for committed usage, reducing EC2/Fargate/Lambda costs.
optionExplanations.D: Broad access increases security risk and does not optimize cost.
optionExplanations.E: Indefinite S3 Standard storage is expensive; lifecycle policies should transition or expire old data.

keyConcept: Cost optimization: stop idle resources and commit to savings plans for predictable use.

question: A financial team needs to understand which AWS services and which internal teams are driving costs. Which AWS tool lets them view spending broken down by service, region, or tag?
explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interactive UI to visualize, understand, and manage AWS costs and usage over time. You can filter and group by service, region, account, or cost allocation tag.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Cost Explorer is the primary tool for visualizing and analysing cost and usage data.
optionExplanations.B: CloudWatch monitors operational metrics like CPU and network, not billing data.
optionExplanations.C: CloudTrail records API activity for auditing, not for financial cost analysis.
optionExplanations.D: AWS Organizations manages multiple accounts and consolidated billing but does not provide Cost Explorer's visualisation.

keyConcept: AWS Cost Explorer: interactive cost/usage visualization with filtering by service, region, tag.

question: A company is preparing a business case to justify migrating from its on-premises data center to AWS. Which financial metric should the leadership team evaluate to compare the total direct and indirect lifetime costs of on-premises infrastructure against AWS Cloud operational expenses?
explanation: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) accounts for all direct costs (servers, storage, network) and indirect costs (power, cooling, floor space, facilities maintenance, and administrative overhead), providing a comprehensive comparison between on-premises ownership and AWS operational expenditure.

optionExplanations.A: Internal Rate of Return measures project profitability rate, not comprehensive infrastructure ownership cost.
optionExplanations.B: Working Capital Ratio measures short-term liquidity, not data center infrastructure costs.
optionExplanations.C: Net Asset Value is an investment fund valuation metric, not an IT infrastructure cost comparison method.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) compares all direct and indirect expenses of on-premises operations against cloud costs.

keyConcept: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): compares all direct and indirect lifetime costs of on-premises IT against cloud operating costs.

question: A company's finance director notices that its on-premises server costs include upfront hardware purchase, ongoing maintenance contracts, power, and cooling. Which term describes these types of fixed, upfront infrastructure costs?
explanation: Capital expenditure (CapEx) refers to upfront investments in physical assets such as servers and networking equipment. On-premises data centers require significant CapEx, whereas cloud shifts spending to variable OpEx.

optionExplanations.A: OpEx refers to ongoing operational costs — what the cloud model uses.
optionExplanations.B: 'Spot expenditure' is not a standard financial term.
optionExplanations.C: Variable expenditure describes costs that change with usage — characteristic of cloud billing.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. CapEx is the upfront, fixed investment in physical infrastructure.

keyConcept: CapEx = upfront fixed costs (servers, data center); OpEx = ongoing variable costs (cloud subscriptions).

question: Which cloud deployment model connects on-premises infrastructure with AWS Cloud, allowing workloads to be distributed across both environments?
explanation: A hybrid cloud deployment connects on-premises (private) infrastructure with public cloud resources, allowing workloads to run in both environments.

optionExplanations.A: Public cloud means all resources are in the cloud provider's infrastructure — no on-premises component.
optionExplanations.B: Private cloud means all resources run in your own data center.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure with public cloud resources.
optionExplanations.D: Multi-cloud uses multiple cloud providers; it doesn't necessarily include on-premises infrastructure.

keyConcept: Hybrid cloud = combination of on-premises + public cloud, connected via VPN or Direct Connect.

question: A company is concerned about data residency compliance when moving to AWS. Which statement is correct about where AWS stores customer data?

options.text: AWS automatically replicates data to all Regions for resilience
Data residency control is only available with Dedicated Hosts
AWS decides the optimal Region for cost minimisation
Customers choose the Region; AWS never moves data outside without consent

explanation: AWS customers choose which Region to store data in, and AWS does not move customer data outside the selected Region without the customer's explicit consent.

optionExplanations.A: Data is not automatically replicated globally; replication is an opt-in feature.
optionExplanations.B: Data residency is a standard feature available to all customers.
optionExplanations.C: AWS does not unilaterally move customer data for cost optimisation.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Customers control which Region data resides in; AWS does not move it without consent.

keyConcept: Data residency: customers choose the Region — AWS never moves data outside that Region without consent.

question: Which TWO statements accurately describe advantages of using AWS Cloud over traditional on-premises infrastructure?

options.text: AWS allows companies to trade fixed capital expenses for variable operational expenses
AWS requires companies to predict capacity needs 3 years in advance
AWS enables organisations to stop spending money guessing at infrastructure capacity
AWS eliminates all customer responsibility for data security
AWS infrastructure is only available in the United States

explanation: Two core cloud advantages: trading CapEx for variable OpEx (pay-as-you-go) and eliminating the need to over- or under-provision by guessing future demand.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Cloud replaces upfront hardware costs with pay-as-you-go expenses.
optionExplanations.B: The cloud eliminates the need to predict years ahead — capacity is elastic and on-demand.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Elastic scaling means you provision what you need when you need it.
optionExplanations.D: Customers retain responsibility for their own data security under the shared responsibility model.
optionExplanations.E: AWS infrastructure spans multiple Regions globally.

keyConcept: Cloud advantages: CapEx → OpEx + stop guessing capacity (elastic, on-demand provisioning).

question: AWS describes one advantage of cloud computing as 'massive economies of scale.' What does this mean for customers?

options.text: Customers must commit to large volumes to receive any pricing
Prices increase as more customers join AWS
Only enterprise-sized customers receive lower prices
AWS aggregated usage enables lower variable costs than most companies could achieve alone

explanation: AWS aggregates usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, enabling massive-scale purchasing and passing savings on as lower variable costs.

optionExplanations.A: Customers pay variable rates with no required volume commitment on On-Demand.
optionExplanations.B: More customers increase AWS's scale and typically lead to lower prices over time.
optionExplanations.C: All AWS customers benefit from economies of scale.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. AWS's scale drives lower per-unit costs passed to all customers.

keyConcept: Economies of scale: AWS aggregates demand → lower per-unit costs for all customers.

question: Which cloud advantage allows a developer to spin up a new testing environment in minutes rather than waiting weeks for IT to procure and rack servers?
explanation: Speed and agility — resources available in minutes — is a key cloud advantage allowing developers to experiment and deploy faster.

optionExplanations.A: High availability refers to minimising downtime, not provisioning speed.
optionExplanations.B: Dedicated hosting is a compute tenancy option, not a cloud advantage.
optionExplanations.C: Disaster recovery describes recovering from failures, not provisioning speed.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Speed and agility: provision resources in minutes vs. weeks.

keyConcept: Speed and agility: provision resources in minutes, enabling faster experimentation and innovation.

question: What is the core definition of cloud computing?

options.text: A specific hardware product sold by cloud vendors
A type of on-premises private data center
On-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing

explanation: Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing, eliminating the need to buy and maintain physical hardware.

optionExplanations.A: Wireless networking standards are network protocols; cloud computing is a delivery model.
optionExplanations.B: Cloud computing is a service model, not a hardware product.
optionExplanations.C: On-premises private data centers are the traditional alternative.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Cloud = on-demand IT resources over the internet, pay-as-you-go.

keyConcept: Cloud computing = on-demand IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing.

question: Which TWO design principles directly support the Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: Deploy all servers in a single Availability Zone
Manually reboot servers during production outages

explanation: Reliability design principles include: automatically recover from failure, test recovery procedures, scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability, stop guessing capacity, and manage change in automation.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Automated recovery based on KPI monitoring is a core Reliability design principle.
optionExplanations.B: Single-AZ deployment creates a single point of failure and violates Reliability.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Testing recovery procedures validates that recovery strategies function as intended.
optionExplanations.D: Manual interventions introduce delays and human error during outages.
optionExplanations.E: Horizontal scaling is recommended to improve workload availability.

keyConcept: Reliability pillar: ability to recover from failures and meet workload requirements consistently.

question: A company wants to review its AWS workloads against Well-Architected best practices using an interactive questionnaire. Which AWS tool provides this?
explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Tool provides a free self-service questionnaire-based review process, generating a report with high-risk findings and improvement recommendations across all six pillars.

optionExplanations.A: Trusted Advisor provides automated checks; it is not an interactive architectural questionnaire.
optionExplanations.B: Config evaluates resource configuration compliance; not an architectural questionnaire.
optionExplanations.C: Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities; it is not an architectural review tool.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. The Well-Architected Tool guides teams through structured reviews.

keyConcept: AWS Well-Architected Tool: free questionnaire-based self-service review across all six pillars.

question: An engineering team wants to understand system health in real time, automate responses to events, and continuously improve through lessons learned from production incidents. Which Well-Architected pillar guides this?
explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving processes through operations as code and learning from failures.

optionExplanations.A: Security focuses on protecting data and systems.
optionExplanations.B: Sustainability focuses on minimising environmental impact.
optionExplanations.C: Reliability focuses on recovery from failures.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Operational Excellence covers monitoring, event response, and continuous improvement.

keyConcept: Operational Excellence: run and monitor systems, learn from failures, improve operations continuously.

question: A company wants to use the most efficient cloud resources, experiment with new instance types, and replace servers with managed services to reduce admin burden. Which Well-Architected pillar focuses on this?
explanation: The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on efficient use of computing resources and leveraging managed and serverless services.

optionExplanations.A: Reliability focuses on fault tolerance and recovery.
optionExplanations.B: Cost Optimization is about eliminating unnecessary costs.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Performance Efficiency covers using resources efficiently and leveraging managed/serverless services.
optionExplanations.D: Operational Excellence is about running and monitoring systems effectively.

keyConcept: Performance Efficiency: use computing resources efficiently; leverage managed services and experiment.

question: An architect wants to reduce the environmental impact of a cloud workload by selecting energy-efficient hardware and minimising idle resources. Which AWS Well-Architected pillar addresses this (added in 2021)?
explanation: The Sustainability pillar, added in 2021, focuses on minimising the environmental impact of cloud workloads through efficient resource use and hardware utilisation maximisation.

optionExplanations.A: Cost Optimization focuses on financial savings, not environmental impact.
optionExplanations.B: Performance Efficiency focuses on resource efficiency for performance, not sustainability.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Sustainability is the sixth pillar focused on reducing the environmental footprint of workloads.
optionExplanations.D: Operational Excellence focuses on operational processes.

keyConcept: Sustainability pillar (6th): minimise environmental impact through efficient resource use.

question: Which TWO design principles belong to the Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: Apply security at all layers of the architecture
Eliminate the need for patches by using containers
Enable traceability by logging and monitoring all actions
Run all workloads in a single AZ for cost efficiency
Manually approve all changes before deployment

explanation: Two core Security pillar design principles: applying security at all layers (defense-in-depth) and enabling traceability through comprehensive logging and monitoring.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Defense-in-depth applies security controls at every architectural layer.
optionExplanations.B: Containers still require patching; this is not a Well-Architected security principle.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Enabling traceability via CloudTrail and CloudWatch Logs is a core security principle.
optionExplanations.D: Single-AZ deployment violates Reliability — it is a single point of failure.
optionExplanations.E: Automation is preferred over manual gates for security and speed.

keyConcept: Security pillar principles: apply security at all layers + enable traceability (logging/monitoring).

question: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar focuses on identifying and eliminating unneeded resources, right-sizing compute, and using the appropriate pricing model to reduce cloud spending?
explanation: The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on eliminating unnecessary costs, right-sizing resources, using managed services, matching capacity to demand, and using savings models.

optionExplanations.A: Security focuses on protecting information and systems.
optionExplanations.B: Performance Efficiency is about resource efficiency for performance, not cost reduction.
optionExplanations.C: Reliability is about recovery and consistent workload operation.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Cost Optimization delivers business value at the lowest price point.

keyConcept: Cost Optimization pillar: right-size, eliminate idle resources, use savings models and managed services.

question: How many pillars make up the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is built on six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.

optionExplanations.A: Four is incorrect.
optionExplanations.B: Five is incorrect — Sustainability was added in 2021 to bring the total to six.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Six pillars: OpEx, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.
optionExplanations.D: Eight is incorrect.

keyConcept: Well-Architected Framework: 6 pillars — OpEx, Security, Reliability, Performance, Cost, Sustainability.

question: Which TWO perspectives are part of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?
explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) organizes guidance into six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The Business perspective ensures cloud investments align with business outcomes.
optionExplanations.B: Hardware manufacturing is not an AWS CAF perspective.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. The Governance perspective focuses on orchestrating cloud initiatives and managing risk.
optionExplanations.D: Desktop publishing is unrelated to cloud adoption strategy.
optionExplanations.E: Real estate is not a CAF perspective.

keyConcept: AWS CAF: 6 perspectives (Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations).

question: In the AWS CAF, which perspective focuses on ensuring cloud strategy delivers business value and stakeholder alignment?
explanation: The Business perspective of the CAF focuses on ensuring IT investments align with business goals and that cloud adoption delivers business value including benefits realisation.

optionExplanations.A: The Platform perspective covers cloud architecture and technology choices.
optionExplanations.B: The Security perspective covers protecting data and meeting compliance requirements.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. The Business perspective aligns cloud investment with business strategy and value delivery.
optionExplanations.D: The Operations perspective covers how cloud operations are managed day-to-day.

keyConcept: CAF Business perspective: aligns cloud investment with business goals and ensures value delivery.

question: Which migration strategy involves moving an application to the cloud with minimal changes — also known as lift-and-shift?
explanation: Rehost (lift-and-shift) means moving an application to the cloud with no changes to the application architecture — the fastest migration strategy.

optionExplanations.A: Replatform makes small cloud optimisations without changing core architecture.
optionExplanations.B: Repurchase replaces the application with a different product (typically SaaS).
optionExplanations.C: Refactor involves significantly redesigning the application for cloud-native features.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Rehost = lift-and-shift with no application changes.

keyConcept: Rehost (lift-and-shift): move to cloud with no application changes — fastest, lowest risk migration.

question: A company decides to switch from its licensed on-premises CRM to a SaaS-based CRM (such as Salesforce). Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Repurchase means replacing an existing application with a commercial off-the-shelf or SaaS alternative.

optionExplanations.A: Rehost moves the same application to cloud infrastructure with no changes.
optionExplanations.B: Replatform makes small cloud optimisations while keeping the same application.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Repurchase replaces the current application with a SaaS equivalent.
optionExplanations.D: Retire decommissions the application because it is no longer needed.

keyConcept: Repurchase: replace existing app with a SaaS alternative (e.g., self-hosted CRM → Salesforce).

question: During an application portfolio review, a company discovers that 20% of its applications are outdated and no longer used. What migration strategy should be applied?
explanation: Retire means decommissioning applications that are no longer needed, reducing migration scope and eliminating unnecessary costs.

optionExplanations.A: Rehost moves applications to the cloud; not appropriate for unused applications.
optionExplanations.B: Retain means keeping applications in their current environment.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Retire = shut down applications that are no longer used.
optionExplanations.D: Relocate moves applications to a different environment; unused apps should be retired.

keyConcept: Retire: decommission unused applications — reduces migration scope and cost.

question: A company wants to redesign a complex monolithic application as cloud-native microservices. This requires significant re-engineering effort. Which migration strategy applies?
explanation: Refactor (Re-architect) involves redesigning the application to fully leverage cloud-native features such as serverless, containers, and managed services.

optionExplanations.A: Rehost moves the same application with no changes.
optionExplanations.B: Replatform makes small optimisations without redesigning the core architecture.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Refactor/Re-architect = significant redesign for cloud-native architecture.
optionExplanations.D: Repurchase replaces the application with a different product.

keyConcept: Refactor/Re-architect: redesign application as cloud-native — most effort, greatest long-term benefit.

question: A company has an application with a compliance requirement mandating it remain on-premises for another 2 years. Which migration strategy applies?
explanation: Retain means keeping the application in its current environment because it is not suitable for migration at this time.

optionExplanations.A: Rehost migrates to the cloud — not appropriate when compliance requires on-premises.
optionExplanations.B: Repurchase replaces with SaaS — doesn't address the on-premises compliance requirement.
optionExplanations.C: Retire decommissions the application — not appropriate for a needed, compliant application.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Retain = keep on-premises for applications not ready or suitable for migration.

keyConcept: Retain: keep on-premises temporarily when migration is not yet feasible (compliance, dependencies).

question: Which TWO AWS services help customers track and manage the progress of a large application migration to AWS?
explanation: AWS Migration Hub provides a central location to track migration progress. AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) automates the lift-and-shift replication and cutover of servers.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Migration Hub aggregates migration status from different tools into a single view.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. AWS MGN automates server replication and cutover for lift-and-shift migrations.
optionExplanations.C: Route 53 is a DNS service; it is not a migration tracking tool.
optionExplanations.D: Budgets tracks costs; it is not a migration service.
optionExplanations.E: Polly converts text to speech; it is unrelated to migration.

keyConcept: Migration Hub (tracks progress) + AWS MGN (automates lift-and-shift server replication).

question: A company wants to migrate its Oracle database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Which AWS service automates the data migration between different database engines?
explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) migrates databases to AWS with minimal downtime, supporting heterogeneous migrations between different database engines.

optionExplanations.A: Snowball is for large-scale physical data transfer, not database schema migration.
optionExplanations.B: Glue is an ETL service for analytics pipelines, not a database migration tool.
optionExplanations.C: DataSync transfers files; it doesn't migrate database schemas or structures.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. DMS automates database replication and migration, including heterogeneous engine migrations.

keyConcept: AWS DMS: migrates databases to AWS with minimal downtime; supports heterogeneous engine migrations.

question: Which migration strategy involves moving workloads to a compatible cloud platform environment — such as VMware on-premises to VMware Cloud on AWS — without changing the application?
explanation: Relocate involves moving infrastructure to a different environment using the same platform (e.g., VMware on-premises to VMware Cloud on AWS) with no changes to the application or operating model.

optionExplanations.A: Rehost (lift-and-shift) typically involves moving to EC2 or similar cloud compute.
optionExplanations.B: Replatform makes cloud optimisations; Relocate keeps the same platform.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Relocate moves the same platform/stack to a compatible cloud environment.
optionExplanations.D: Refactor redesigns the application for cloud-native architecture.

keyConcept: Relocate: move workloads using same platform (e.g., VMware on-prem → VMware Cloud on AWS).

question: A company wants to identify EC2 instances running at very low CPU utilisation that could be downsized to reduce cost. Which AWS service provides ML-based rightsizing recommendations?
explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyse utilisation metrics and recommend rightsizing or instance type changes that reduce cost without sacrificing performance.

optionExplanations.A: Budgets sets cost thresholds; it doesn't analyse utilisation for rightsizing.
optionExplanations.B: Organizations manages accounts; it doesn't analyse instance utilisation.
optionExplanations.C: CloudWatch monitors metrics; it doesn't generate rightsizing recommendations.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Compute Optimizer provides ML-based rightsizing recommendations.

keyConcept: AWS Compute Optimizer: ML-based rightsizing — reduces wasted spend on oversized resources.

question: A company has unused Standard Reserved Instances after its usage patterns changed. Which AWS feature lets them sell these to other AWS customers?
explanation: The AWS Reserved Instance Marketplace allows customers to sell unused Standard Reserved Instances to other AWS customers.

optionExplanations.A: Budgets is a cost alert tool; it has no RI exchange feature.
optionExplanations.B: Service Quotas manages service limits; it has no RI listing feature.
optionExplanations.C: Cost Explorer is a cost visualisation tool; it cannot transfer RIs.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. The RI Marketplace lets customers sell unused Standard RIs.

keyConcept: Reserved Instance Marketplace: sell unused Standard RIs to other AWS customers to recoup costs.

question: Which concept refers to the total financial impact — including hardware, facilities, staffing, power, and cooling — of owning IT infrastructure on-premises?
explanation: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) includes all direct and indirect costs of owning and operating on-premises infrastructure — used to build the business case for cloud migration.

optionExplanations.A: OpEx covers ongoing operational costs but doesn't capture the full indirect cost of ownership.
optionExplanations.B: Run rate refers to current ongoing cost; not the comprehensive TCO concept.
optionExplanations.C: NPV is a financial metric measuring value of future cash flows — an output of TCO analysis.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. TCO captures all costs of owning and operating infrastructure vs. equivalent cloud cost.

keyConcept: TCO = all costs of owning IT (hardware, facilities, staffing, power) vs. equivalent cloud cost.

question: Which S3 pricing model automatically reduces per-unit cost as total usage grows, without requiring a commitment?
explanation: Amazon S3 uses tiered pricing where per-GB cost automatically decreases as total monthly storage volume increases — no commitment required.

optionExplanations.A: Spot pricing applies to EC2, not S3.
optionExplanations.B: Reserved capacity requires a commitment; tiered pricing doesn't.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Volume-based tiered pricing automatically reduces per-unit cost as usage grows.
optionExplanations.D: S3 uses tiered pricing with decreasing rates, not a flat rate.

keyConcept: Volume-based tiered pricing: per-unit cost decreases as usage grows — no commitment needed.

question: Which major on-premises cost does the cloud eliminate for customers by managing all physical infrastructure operations?

options.text: Undifferentiated heavy lifting — managing physical infrastructure, power, cooling, and facilities

explanation: AWS handles all physical infrastructure management — hardware procurement, data center operations, power, cooling, and physical security — so customers can focus on applications rather than infrastructure work.

optionExplanations.A: Software licensing still applies on AWS for many products.
optionExplanations.B: Internet bandwidth costs still apply; AWS charges for data transfer out.
optionExplanations.C: Application development costs remain the customer's responsibility.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Cloud eliminates undifferentiated heavy lifting — no more managing physical infrastructure.

keyConcept: Cloud eliminates undifferentiated heavy lifting: no more managing physical servers, power, cooling, or facilities.

question: Which Reliability pillar design principle states that workloads should monitor KPIs and trigger automated recovery when thresholds are breached?
explanation: The Reliability pillar's 'Automatically recover from failure' principle states workloads should monitor KPIs and trigger automated recovery when thresholds are breached.

optionExplanations.A: 'Perform operations as code' is an Operational Excellence principle.
optionExplanations.B: Loose coupling is an architectural pattern, not a named Well-Architected design principle.
optionExplanations.C: 'Implement observability' is an Operational Excellence principle.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Auto-recovery is a core Reliability design principle.

keyConcept: Reliability principle: automatically recover from failure — KPI monitoring triggers automated healing.

question: An architect proposes testing disaster recovery procedures in production regularly to build confidence in recovery. Which Reliability design principle does this align with?
explanation: 'Test recovery procedures' is a named Reliability pillar design principle — organisations should test recovery in non-production and production to validate it works as expected.

optionExplanations.A: Horizontal scaling improves availability; it doesn't specifically involve testing recovery.
optionExplanations.B: Stop guessing capacity is also a Reliability principle but relates to scaling.
optionExplanations.C: Using automation is an Operational Excellence principle.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Testing recovery procedures is a named Reliability pillar design principle.

keyConcept: Reliability principle: test recovery procedures regularly — don't assume recovery works until tested.

question: Which AWS service provides a centralised location to plan and track migrations of on-premises applications, integrating with AWS Application Discovery Service and partner tools?
explanation: AWS Migration Hub provides a centralised location to plan and track migration progress, integrating with Application Discovery Service and multiple AWS and partner migration tools.

optionExplanations.A: DataSync transfers files; it is not a migration planning hub.
optionExplanations.B: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities; it is not a migration management service.
optionExplanations.C: Control Tower governs multi-account environments; it is not a migration tool.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Migration Hub centralises migration planning, tracking, and visibility.

keyConcept: AWS Migration Hub: centralised planning and tracking of on-premises to AWS migrations.

question: Which migration strategy involves making small cloud optimisations — such as switching to a managed database service — without changing the core application code?
explanation: Replatform (lift-tinker-and-shift) involves targeted optimisations during migration — such as moving a database to Amazon RDS — to take advantage of cloud capabilities without redesigning the application.

optionExplanations.A: Rehost moves the application with zero changes.
optionExplanations.B: Retire decommissions the application.
optionExplanations.C: Refactor redesigns the application significantly.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Replatform makes small cloud optimisations without core code changes.

keyConcept: Replatform: small cloud optimisations (e.g., move to RDS) without changing core application code.

question: A company wants to run AWS services on-premises for data-sensitive workloads that cannot leave its facility. Which AWS service extends AWS infrastructure to on-premises locations?
explanation: AWS Outposts delivers fully managed AWS infrastructure and services on-premises, allowing customers to run compute and storage locally while connecting to the AWS cloud region for management.

optionExplanations.A: Direct Connect provides a private network link to AWS; it doesn't run AWS services on-premises.
optionExplanations.B: Wavelength extends AWS to 5G network edges for mobile applications.
optionExplanations.C: Local Zones extend AWS to specific metro areas — not on-premises in the customer's facility.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Outposts extends AWS infrastructure into on-premises data centers.

keyConcept: AWS Outposts: AWS infrastructure and services in your on-premises facility — hybrid cloud consistency.

question: Which cloud computing model provides complete applications over the internet where the provider manages everything including infrastructure, platform, and application?
explanation: SaaS delivers complete applications over the internet managed entirely by the provider (e.g., Gmail, Salesforce). Customers just use the software; the provider handles everything else.

optionExplanations.A: IaaS provides virtualised compute, storage, and networking (e.g., Amazon EC2).
optionExplanations.B: PaaS provides a platform for developing and deploying applications without managing infrastructure.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. SaaS is a fully managed application delivered over the internet.
optionExplanations.D: FaaS like AWS Lambda is a compute model, not a full application delivery model.

keyConcept: SaaS: fully managed application delivered over the internet — provider manages everything.

question: Which cloud computing model gives customers the most control over the operating system and networking, while the provider manages physical hardware?
explanation: IaaS provides virtualised computing resources over the internet. Customers control the OS and above; the provider manages the physical hardware.

optionExplanations.A: SaaS delivers complete applications; customers control nothing below the application.
optionExplanations.B: PaaS provides a development platform; customers control the application but not the OS.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. IaaS (e.g., EC2) gives customers OS-level control while provider manages physical hardware.
optionExplanations.D: Database as a Service is a subset of PaaS; the provider manages the database engine.

keyConcept: IaaS: customers control OS and above; provider manages physical hardware (EC2 is an example).

question: Which AWS Well-Architected pillar recommends using MFA, fine-grained access controls, and protecting data at rest and in transit?
explanation: The Security pillar covers identity and access management, detective controls, infrastructure protection, and data protection — including MFA, least privilege, and encryption.

optionExplanations.A: Operational Excellence covers running and monitoring systems effectively.
optionExplanations.B: Reliability covers recovery from failures.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Security covers IAM, encryption, access controls, MFA, and incident response.
optionExplanations.D: Performance Efficiency covers efficient use of resources.

keyConcept: Security pillar: IAM, MFA, least privilege, encryption in transit and at rest, incident response.

question: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) identifies four cloud transformation outcomes. Which TWO are among them?
explanation: The AWS CAF describes four cloud transformation outcomes: reduced cost, improved resilience, increased revenue, and accelerated business transformation/innovation.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Reduced cost is one of the four CAF business outcomes.
optionExplanations.B: Improved resilience is a CAF outcome, but 'only' makes this option incomplete as a CAF outcome description.
optionExplanations.C: Security responsibilities are shared; they are never eliminated.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Accelerated digitalisation and business transformation is a CAF outcome.
optionExplanations.E: AWS provides high availability but 100% uptime cannot be guaranteed.

keyConcept: CAF transformation outcomes: reduced cost, improved resilience, increased revenue, accelerated transformation.

question: Which AWS service provides pre-built dashboards, graphs, and filtering capabilities for understanding, managing, and forecasting AWS costs?
explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interactive console experience with pre-built views, filtering by service/region/account/tag, and 12-month forecasting.

optionExplanations.A: Budgets alerts when thresholds are crossed; it is not a visualisation and exploration tool.
optionExplanations.B: Pricing Calculator estimates future costs for planned architectures.
optionExplanations.C: CUR provides raw detailed data in CSV/S3; it requires additional tooling to visualise.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Cost Explorer provides pre-built dashboards and interactive filtering for cost analysis.

keyConcept: AWS Cost Explorer: pre-built dashboards for interactive cost analysis and forecasting.

question: A company has very heavy traffic on weekdays but near-zero on weekends. On-premises they size for peak. In the cloud they scale down on weekends. Which cloud economic principle enables this?

options.text: Matching supply to demand through elasticity

explanation: Elasticity allows cloud resources to scale in and out to match demand. Unlike on-premises where you pay for peak capacity, cloud billing matches actual consumption.

optionExplanations.A: Economies of scale reduce per-unit costs — not specifically about demand matching.
optionExplanations.B: Managed services simplify operations; they don't directly describe demand-matching billing.
optionExplanations.C: Global reach refers to deploying in multiple Regions.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Elasticity: scale up when demand is high, scale down and save when demand drops.

keyConcept: Elasticity: match supply to actual demand — pay for what you use, not peak capacity.

question: A company runs all its resources in the AWS Cloud and does not own any physical servers or data centers. Which cloud deployment model does this represent?
explanation: A public cloud (all-in-cloud) deployment means all components run in the cloud — no on-premises hardware. AWS is a public cloud provider.

optionExplanations.A: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises with cloud; this company has no on-premises infrastructure.
optionExplanations.B: Private cloud uses dedicated infrastructure in the company's own facility.
optionExplanations.C: Multi-cloud uses multiple cloud providers; the question only describes AWS.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. All resources in the cloud with no on-premises component = all-in-cloud.

keyConcept: All-in-cloud (public cloud): all resources in the cloud — no on-premises hardware.

question: Which Operational Excellence design principle recommends making many small, reversible changes rather than large infrequent updates to reduce the blast radius of failures?

options.text: Avoid all changes once in production

explanation: 'Make frequent, small, reversible changes' is an Operational Excellence principle. Small changes are easier to test, review, and roll back, reducing risk compared to large releases.

optionExplanations.A: Large batch changes increase risk; small changes are recommended.
optionExplanations.B: Testing in production safely (canary, blue/green) is also encouraged.
optionExplanations.C: Avoiding all changes is not feasible; frequent small changes enable continuous improvement.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Small, reversible changes reduce risk and enable rapid rollback.

keyConcept: Operational Excellence: frequent, small, reversible changes — reduce blast radius, enable quick rollback.

question: A company is paying On-Demand rates for EC2 instances that have been running continuously for over 12 months. Which action would reduce this cost immediately?

options.text: Move the instances to a different Region
Terminate the instances and rebuild them each month
Purchase Reserved Instances or Compute Savings Plans for that workload

explanation: Instances running 24/7 for long periods are ideal candidates for Reserved Instances or Savings Plans, which can reduce costs by up to 72% compared to On-Demand.

optionExplanations.A: Changing Regions changes latency and may not reduce cost.
optionExplanations.B: Billing reports improve visibility but don't reduce costs.
optionExplanations.C: Terminating and rebuilding achieves nothing — On-Demand charges accumulate regardless.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Long-running steady-state workloads benefit significantly from commitment-based pricing.

keyConcept: Long-running steady workloads: purchase RIs or Savings Plans for up to 72% off On-Demand rates.

question: Which AWS governance mechanism enforces resource standards and prevents developers from provisioning unapproved instance types across all accounts in an organisation?

options.text: AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations

explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations set guardrails that restrict the actions allowed in member accounts — they can prevent provisioning specific or unapproved instance types.

optionExplanations.A: Cost Explorer alerts on spending; it cannot prevent resource creation.
optionExplanations.B: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations; it cannot enforce policies.
optionExplanations.C: CloudWatch billing alarms alert after the fact; they cannot prevent provisioning.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. SCPs set guardrails preventing disallowed actions in member accounts.

keyConcept: SCPs: guardrails that prevent disallowed actions (e.g., unapproved instance types) across all org accounts.

question: A company identifies applications that are too complex to migrate now and will require 18+ more months on-premises. Which of the 7 Rs applies?
explanation: Retain means keeping the application in its current on-premises environment because it is not yet ready or suitable for migration.

optionExplanations.A: Retire decommissions unused or unnecessary applications.
optionExplanations.B: Repurchase replaces with a SaaS equivalent.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Retain = keep on-premises temporarily; revisit migration later.
optionExplanations.D: Rehost lifts and shifts to cloud — the application is not ready.

keyConcept: Retain: keep application on-premises when not ready for migration — revisit later.

question: Which AWS Well-Architected concept suggests workloads should be designed so a single point of failure does not cause the entire system to fail?
explanation: Eliminating single points of failure (SPOF) is a core Reliability pillar design pattern — redundancy at each layer prevents a single failure from taking down the entire system.

optionExplanations.A: Vertical scaling increases a single server's size; it doesn't eliminate SPOF.
optionExplanations.B: A single-server architecture is itself a single point of failure.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Eliminating SPOF through redundancy is a fundamental Reliability principle.
