optionExplanations.D: Synchronous coupling creates tight dependencies that can cascade failures.

keyConcept: Eliminate single points of failure: add redundancy at each layer so no single failure takes down the system.

question: In the AWS Cloud, which party is responsible for physical hardware maintenance — servers, networking, and data center facilities?

options.text: Both AWS and the customer jointly

explanation: AWS is responsible for all physical hardware and the physical security of its data centers. This is the 'security of the cloud' side of the shared responsibility model.

optionExplanations.A: Customers are responsible for security 'in the cloud' — OS, applications, data — not physical hardware.
optionExplanations.B: Physical hardware maintenance is exclusively AWS's responsibility.
optionExplanations.C: Hardware vendors sell equipment but don't maintain it in production on behalf of customers.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. AWS owns, operates, and maintains all physical infrastructure.

keyConcept: AWS responsibility: physical hardware, facilities, and global network infrastructure.

question: A team accidentally launched hundreds of EC2 instances in a test account that were never terminated, causing an unexpectedly large bill. Which AWS feature could have triggered an early warning?

options.text: AWS Budgets with a cost or usage alert

explanation: AWS Budgets can set thresholds on cost or instance count (usage) and send alerts when the threshold is breached or forecast to be breached — enabling early warning before costs grow further.

optionExplanations.A: Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deployment; it doesn't alert on live spending.
optionExplanations.B: CloudTrail records API activity; it doesn't send billing alerts.
optionExplanations.C: CloudWatch logs record events; it doesn't send billing alerts by default.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Budgets alerts when EC2 cost or instance count exceeds a threshold.

keyConcept: AWS Budgets: cost or usage alerts — early warning when spending or resource count exceeds threshold.

question: Which cloud advantage enables a company to stop spending on data center operations and redirect resources toward customer-facing innovation?

options.text: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Trade variable expense for fixed expense
Maintain dedicated hardware for peak load

explanation: 'Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers' is one of the six cloud advantages. AWS manages infrastructure so customers can focus on differentiating their business.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. This is AWS advantage #5: stop spending on undifferentiated infrastructure management.
optionExplanations.B: Cloud trades fixed CapEx for variable OpEx — the opposite of this option.
optionExplanations.C: Cloud can simplify compliance; it doesn't increase requirements.
optionExplanations.D: Dedicated hardware for peak load is an on-premises anti-pattern; cloud uses elastic capacity.

keyConcept: Cloud advantage: stop spending on data center operations — redirect resources to innovation.

question: Which TWO Well-Architected pillars deal primarily with: (1) running and operating systems effectively, and (2) protecting data and systems?
explanation: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems, while Security focuses on protecting data and systems.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Operational Excellence: run and monitor systems, learn from failures.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Security: protect data and systems at every layer.
optionExplanations.C: Sustainability focuses on minimising environmental impact.
optionExplanations.D: Cost Optimization focuses on eliminating unnecessary spending.
optionExplanations.E: Reliability focuses on recovery from failures.

keyConcept: Operational Excellence = run and operate systems; Security = protect data and systems.

question: In which phase of a cloud migration journey does a company discover its application portfolio, assess readiness, and build a business case?
explanation: The Assess phase is the first phase: discover the application portfolio, understand TCO, assess readiness, and determine migration priorities and strategies.

optionExplanations.A: The Migrate and Modernize phase involves executing migrations at scale.
optionExplanations.B: The Mobilize phase involves building the cloud foundation (landing zone) and running pilots.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Assess is the first phase: discover, evaluate, prioritise, and build the business case.
optionExplanations.D: Decommission (Retire) happens after migration — not a formal migration phase.

keyConcept: Migration phases: Assess (discover + prioritise) → Mobilize (foundation + pilots) → Migrate and Modernize.

question: Which AWS statement best explains how economies of scale result in lower pricing for customers?

options.text: AWS charges the same price regardless of volume
AWS negotiates prices individually per customer
AWS charges more as usage increases
AWS passes on lower per-unit costs due to aggregated purchasing across hundreds of thousands of customers

explanation: AWS aggregates demand from hundreds of thousands of customers, achieving massive economies of scale and passing savings on as lower variable pricing.

optionExplanations.A: Per-unit costs decrease with volume due to tiered pricing — not the same price.
optionExplanations.B: Standard service pricing is published publicly.
optionExplanations.C: Per-unit costs decrease, not increase, as usage grows.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. AWS passes on cost savings from massive scale to all customers.

keyConcept: Economies of scale: AWS aggregates demand → lower per-unit costs for all customers.

question: Dev/test EC2 instances are running 24/7 but are only used during business hours. Which cost optimisation action would save the most money?

options.text: Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances for these environments
Enable detailed monitoring for all instances
Move the environments to Dedicated Hosts
Use AWS Instance Scheduler to automatically stop instances outside business hours

explanation: Scheduling start/stop for non-production instances saves compute costs for the 16+ idle hours per day — typically reducing cost by 60%+ for business-hours-only environments.

optionExplanations.A: 3-year RIs are for 24/7 steady-state workloads; purchasing them for part-time environments wastes money.
optionExplanations.B: Detailed monitoring improves visibility but doesn't reduce idle compute costs.
optionExplanations.C: Dedicated Hosts are for licensing compliance and are more expensive.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Scheduling auto start/stop can reduce dev instance costs by 60%+.

keyConcept: Schedule dev instances: auto start/stop outside business hours — significant cost savings.

question: Which type of cloud model is provisioned for exclusive use by a single organisation?
explanation: A private cloud is cloud infrastructure provisioned for exclusive use by a single organisation, either managed internally or by a third party.

optionExplanations.A: Public cloud is shared among many customers (multi-tenant).
optionExplanations.B: Community cloud is shared by several organisations with similar requirements.
optionExplanations.C: Hybrid cloud combines private and public cloud environments.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Private cloud is exclusively dedicated to one organisation.

keyConcept: Private cloud: exclusively for one organisation — managed on-premises or by a third party.

question: Which Well-Architected design principle recommends using serverless or managed services to remove operational burden?

options.text: Operational Excellence: perform operations as code
Cost Optimization: adopt a consumption model

explanation: The Performance Efficiency pillar includes 'use serverless architectures' and 'use managed services' design principles, reducing the operational burden of managing servers.

optionExplanations.A: 'Perform operations as code' is Operational Excellence — automating operations.
optionExplanations.B: 'Adopt a consumption model' is a Cost Optimization principle.
optionExplanations.C: Automatic recovery is a Reliability principle about fault tolerance.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Performance Efficiency recommends serverless and managed services to remove server management overhead.

keyConcept: Performance Efficiency: use serverless architectures and managed services to eliminate server management.

question: A company applies cost allocation tags to EC2 instances but they don't appear in billing reports. Where must the team activate these tags?

options.text: AWS Billing and Cost Management console

explanation: Cost allocation tags must be activated in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console before they appear in billing reports and Cost Explorer — applying a tag in EC2 alone is insufficient.

optionExplanations.A: CloudWatch is for monitoring; it doesn't manage billing tag activation.
optionExplanations.B: Tags can be applied in the EC2 console but activation for billing must happen in the Billing console.
optionExplanations.C: Config tracks resource configurations; it doesn't manage billing tag activation.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Cost allocation tags are activated in the Billing and Cost Management console.

keyConcept: Cost allocation tags: must be activated in Billing console to appear in billing reports and Cost Explorer.

question: What does 'increased speed and agility' mean for software development teams in the context of cloud computing?

options.text: Developers can access new IT resources within minutes rather than weeks
AWS increases the clock speed of processors
All deployments happen without testing or review
IT teams no longer need to write code — AWS generates it

explanation: Increased speed and agility means developers can provision and access new cloud resources in minutes, vs. weeks or months of on-premises hardware procurement.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Cloud: provision new resources in minutes vs. weeks of on-premises procurement.
optionExplanations.B: AWS does not modify processor clock speeds for customers.
optionExplanations.C: Testing remains important; agility means faster iteration.
optionExplanations.D: AWS provides tools; developers still write application code.

keyConcept: Speed and agility: provision new resources in minutes vs. weeks of on-premises procurement.

question: Which AWS service discovers on-premises servers and application dependencies, including configuration and usage data, to prepare for migration?
explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects and presents configuration, usage, and dependency data about on-premises servers through agent-based or agentless discovery.

optionExplanations.A: Migration Hub is the centralised tracking hub; Application Discovery Service feeds data into it.
optionExplanations.B: AWS Server Migration Service (SMS) is deprecated and replaced by AWS Application Migration Service (MGN).
optionExplanations.C: DataSync transfers files; it doesn't discover server configurations.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Application Discovery Service discovers on-premises servers, usage data, and application dependencies.

keyConcept: AWS Application Discovery Service: discover on-premises servers, dependencies, and usage for migration planning.

question: An EC2 instance has been running at less than 5% CPU utilisation for 30 days. Which AWS service identifies this as a cost optimisation opportunity?
explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor's Cost Optimization checks flag underutilised instances — including those with consistently low CPU utilisation — for rightsizing or termination.

optionExplanations.A: CloudWatch collects metrics; it doesn't generate rightsizing or cost recommendations.
optionExplanations.B: The Billing Dashboard shows total charges; it doesn't provide instance-level recommendations.
optionExplanations.C: Cost Explorer shows spending trends; it doesn't proactively flag specific underutilised instances.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Trusted Advisor's Cost Optimization checks flag underutilised instances for action.

keyConcept: Trusted Advisor Cost Optimization: flags idle/underutilised EC2 instances for rightsizing or termination.

question: A company wants to quickly spin up testing environments for its development teams and terminate them when testing completes, avoiding paying for idle servers. Which AWS Cloud benefit best describes this capability?
explanation: Agility in the cloud refers to the speed and ease with which organizations can provision, test, and decommission computing resources, accelerating innovation.

optionExplanations.A: Multi-tenancy refers to sharing underlying infrastructure with other customers, not provisioning speed.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Agility allows teams to experiment rapidly by quickly provisioning and releasing resources.
optionExplanations.C: AWS does not provide customers with physical access to its server hardware.
optionExplanations.D: The cloud replaces fixed costs with variable consumption-based expenses.

keyConcept: Cloud Agility: ability to quickly provision and tear down compute resources to innovate faster.

question: Which TWO options represent core advantages of cloud computing over traditional on-premises infrastructure according to AWS?

options.text: Trade capital expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Full physical control of underlying data center hardware
Elimination of all operating system patching responsibilities

explanation: Two of the six key advantages of cloud computing identified by AWS are trading capital expense for variable expense and benefiting from massive economies of scale.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Instead of investing heavily in data centers upfront, customers pay only for what they use.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Usage from hundreds of thousands of customers aggregates, translating into higher economies of scale and lower pay-as-you-go prices.
optionExplanations.C: Customers do not manage or control the physical data center hardware in AWS.
optionExplanations.D: Data transfer is not entirely free; outbound data transfer charges generally apply.
optionExplanations.E: Customers still manage guest OS patching on services like EC2.

keyConcept: Six Advantages of Cloud: CapEx to variable expense, economies of scale, stop guessing capacity, increase speed/agility, stop spending money running data centers, go global in minutes.

question: An e-commerce business experiences a 10x traffic spike during holiday flash sales and wants server capacity to expand automatically to handle load and shrink when traffic subsides. Which cloud concept does this represent?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability of cloud computing infrastructure to dynamically scale compute capacity up or down in response to real-time changes in demand.

optionExplanations.A: Reliability is the ability of a system to recover from infrastructure disruptions and function correctly.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Elasticity allows resources to automatically match demand fluctuations, avoiding over-provisioning.
optionExplanations.C: Durability refers to long-term data preservation without loss or corruption.
optionExplanations.D: Latency is the time required for a packet to travel across a network.

keyConcept: Elasticity: automatically scaling compute resources up or down to match demand and optimize costs.

question: A gaming company requires its backend services to remain operational even if an entire physical data center encounters a major power failure. Which design choice satisfies this requirement within a single AWS Region?

options.text: Deploying workloads across multiple Availability Zones
Configuring a single larger EC2 instance size
Purchasing Reserved Instances with upfront payment
Placing all servers in a single private subnet

explanation: Availability Zones within an AWS Region are physically separate facilities with independent power, cooling, and network connectivity. Deploying across multiple AZs ensures high availability if one AZ fails.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Multiple AZs provide fault isolation against data center power outages and equipment failures.
optionExplanations.B: Increasing instance size vertically does not protect against host or facility failures.
optionExplanations.C: Reserved Instances are a financial pricing option, not an architectural fault-tolerance mechanism.
optionExplanations.D: A single subnet resides within one AZ and fails if that AZ encounters an outage.

keyConcept: Multi-AZ deployment: provides fault tolerance by isolating workloads across independent data center facilities.

question: Which advantage of the AWS Cloud eliminates the need for organizations to forecast server demands months in advance before purchasing physical hardware?
explanation: 'Stop guessing capacity' is an advantage of cloud computing that lets customers access as much or as little capacity as needed, scaling up and down with only a few minutes notice.

optionExplanations.A: Data replication relates to storage durability, not capacity forecasting.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. On-demand cloud provisioning eliminates the need to predict capacity needs in advance.
optionExplanations.C: AWS is consumption-based cloud computing, not physical hardware leasing.
optionExplanations.D: Compliance certifications validate regulatory adherence, not compute provisioning.

keyConcept: Stop guessing capacity: scale resources dynamically instead of over-provisioning or under-provisioning hardware.

question: A software vendor can launch applications to customers in Asia, Europe, and North America in minutes without signing long-term data center leases abroad. Which cloud benefit does this illustrate?
explanation: AWS global infrastructure spans multiple geographic Regions, allowing customers to deploy applications worldwide in minutes to deliver lower latency and a better user experience.

optionExplanations.A: Data sovereignty requirements remain applicable and must be respected by customers.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Deploying across multiple Regions worldwide in minutes is one of the six advantages of cloud computing.
optionExplanations.C: Cloud compute is billed based on consumption; it is not free.
optionExplanations.D: Cloud infrastructure does not rewrite application source code automatically.

keyConcept: Go global in minutes: deploy applications in multiple AWS Regions worldwide with minimal effort.

question: How does the AWS Cloud enable cost savings through massive economies of scale?

options.text: By allowing customers to negotiate custom hardware contracts with manufacturers
By aggregating usage from hundreds of thousands of customers into lower pay-as-you-go prices
By eliminating the need for security controls
By mandating multi-year locked commitments for all services

explanation: Because AWS aggregates computing usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, it achieves higher economies of scale, translating into lower pay-as-you-go pricing.

optionExplanations.A: AWS manages all hardware procurement; individual customers do not negotiate with manufacturers.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. High aggregate volume lowers overall infrastructure procurement and operational costs.
optionExplanations.C: Security is non-negotiable and shared between AWS and the customer.
optionExplanations.D: Many AWS services operate strictly on-demand without long-term contracts.

keyConcept: Economies of scale: high aggregated customer volume enables AWS to lower pay-as-you-go prices.

question: A company wants its critical financial application to continue operating without interruption even when an individual server hardware component fails. Which architectural property does this demonstrate?
explanation: Fault tolerance is the property that enables a system to continue operating without interruption in the event of failure of one or more of its components.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Fault-tolerant systems withstand component degradation without human intervention or service outage.
optionExplanations.B: Agility refers to speed of deployment and technological experimentation.
optionExplanations.C: Cost optimization focuses on eliminating unnecessary spending.
optionExplanations.D: Elasticity is adjusting resource capacity dynamically based on load.

keyConcept: Fault tolerance: the ability of a workload to remain fully operational during component failures.

question: Which term describes moving funds from heavy upfront physical asset purchases (such as servers, racks, and cooling) to ongoing operational costs based on actual consumption?

options.text: Trading capital expense for variable expense

explanation: Trading capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense (OpEx) is a core advantage of cloud computing, substituting large upfront investments with low pay-as-you-go costs.

optionExplanations.A: Depreciation is an accounting schedule for physical assets.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Customers pay variable expenses for compute and storage rather than upfront capital expenses.
optionExplanations.C: Licensing amortization is an accounting technique, not an AWS cloud advantage.
optionExplanations.D: Capacity reservation reserves compute capacity in an Availability Zone.

keyConcept: CapEx to OpEx: replacing upfront infrastructure capital expenses with pay-as-you-go variable expenses.

question: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving processes and procedures?
explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems, and continually improving processes and procedures to deliver business value.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Operational Excellence encompasses automated deployments, operations as code, and learning from failures.
optionExplanations.B: Reliability focuses on recovering from disruptions and meeting demand.
optionExplanations.C: Performance Efficiency focuses on structured use of computing resources to meet requirements.
optionExplanations.D: Sustainability focuses on minimizing environmental impacts of running cloud workloads.

keyConcept: Operational Excellence Pillar: run/monitor systems, automate operations, and continually refine procedures.

question: A company wants to minimize the environmental impact of its cloud workloads by reducing energy consumption and maximizing resource utilization. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar addresses this goal?
explanation: The Sustainability pillar focuses on environmental impacts, particularly energy consumption and efficiency, encouraging architects to maximize resource utilization and adopt efficient shared services.

optionExplanations.A: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary financial expenditure, not environmental impact.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Sustainability addresses the environmental footprint of cloud workloads.
optionExplanations.C: Security focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets.
optionExplanations.D: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring workloads effectively.

keyConcept: Sustainability Pillar: minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads.

question: When designing cloud workloads aligned with the Performance Efficiency pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which TWO strategies should an organization adopt? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Democratize advanced technologies by consuming them as services
Go global in minutes by deploying across multiple AWS Regions
Manually provision peak capacity to avoid automated autoscaling
Avoid using serverless architectures and containerized runtimes
Perform all system deployments manually during business hours

explanation: Key design principles for the Performance Efficiency pillar include: democratize advanced technologies, go global in minutes, use serverless architectures, experiment more often, and consider mechanical sympathy.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Democratizing advanced technologies lets teams consume complex capabilities (like ML or NoSQL) as managed services without needing to become experts in managing infrastructure.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Going global in minutes enables deploying applications in multiple Regions to provide lower latency and better user experience.
optionExplanations.C: Manually provisioning peak capacity is anti-efficient; systems should scale dynamically.
optionExplanations.D: Serverless architectures are recommended by the Performance Efficiency pillar to remove operational compute overhead.
optionExplanations.E: Manual deployments are error-prone and contradict operational excellence and performance automation.

keyConcept: Performance Efficiency principles: democratize advanced technologies, go global in minutes, and use serverless architectures.

question: Which Well-Architected design principle advocates using temporary credentials, applying least privilege, and protecting data in transit and at rest?
explanation: The Security pillar includes principles such as implementing a strong identity foundation (least privilege, IAM roles), enabling traceability, protecting data at rest and in transit, and preparing for security events.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The Security pillar protects information and systems through confidentiality and integrity controls.
optionExplanations.B: Performance Efficiency focuses on selecting the right resource types and scaling efficiently.
optionExplanations.C: Operational Excellence focuses on monitoring, automating changes, and learning from post-mortems.
optionExplanations.D: Cost Optimization focuses on matching supply with demand and analyzing expenditure.

keyConcept: Security Pillar: protect information, systems, and assets while delivering business value through risk assessments and mitigation strategies.

question: A company replaces self-managed MySQL database instances running on Amazon EC2 with Amazon Aurora Serverless to eliminate manual patching and server provisioning. Which Well-Architected design principle does this follow?

options.text: Use managed services to reduce operational burden

explanation: Using managed services (like Amazon Aurora or AWS Fargate) removes administrative overhead (such as patching OS and managing hardware), freeing teams to focus on application business logic.

optionExplanations.A: A consumption model relates to paying only for resources consumed, while this scenario emphasizes eliminating manual operations.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Managed services offload undifferentiated heavy lifting to AWS.
optionExplanations.C: Traceability involves logging and auditing actions.
optionExplanations.D: Operations as code involves defining procedures as code templates.

keyConcept: Managed Services: offload undifferentiated operational tasks like hardware maintenance and database patching to AWS.

question: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework guides organizations on measuring efficiency, adopting consumption models, and analyzing expenditure over time?
explanation: The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs by understanding spending, selecting appropriate resources, analyzing expenditure, and scaling to meet business needs without overspending.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Cost Optimization focuses on spending efficiency, pricing models, and monitoring expenditure.
optionExplanations.B: Reliability focuses on fault tolerance and system recovery.
optionExplanations.C: Sustainability focuses on reducing energy footprint.
optionExplanations.D: Security focuses on protecting data and identity management.

keyConcept: Cost Optimization Pillar: running systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point.

question: Which AWS tool provides a guided questionnaire to review your cloud architecture against the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Tool helps review workloads against the six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework and provides actionable guidance to improve cloud architectures.

optionExplanations.A: Trusted Advisor inspects your live AWS environment against best practices, but does not provide the guided workload review tool.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. The AWS Well-Architected Tool provides structured milestone reviews against framework questions.
optionExplanations.C: Systems Manager is an operational management hub for configuring and running commands on resources.
optionExplanations.D: AWS Health Dashboard communicates events affecting your specific AWS resources.

keyConcept: AWS Well-Architected Tool: provides structured architectural reviews against the six Well-Architected pillars.

question: A financial organization needs to trace and audit every administrative action performed in its AWS environment. Which design principle from the Security pillar does this align with?
explanation: Enabling traceability means monitoring, alerting, and auditing actions and changes to environment configurations in real-time using logging services like AWS CloudTrail.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Enabling traceability logs and tracks user and system actions for accountability and auditing.
optionExplanations.B: Automating security best practices refers to automated response mechanisms.
optionExplanations.C: Applying security at all layers refers to defense-in-depth across VPC, OS, application, and IAM.
optionExplanations.D: Protecting data in transit refers to encryption over networks (HTTPS/TLS).

keyConcept: Enable traceability: log, monitor, and audit administrative actions and resource changes in real time.

question: Which design principle under the Performance Efficiency pillar recommends selecting technologies (compute, storage, database, network) based on workload requirements rather than a one-size-fits-all approach?
explanation: Mechanical sympathy means having an understanding of how cloud technologies operate and selecting the right services (e.g., NoSQL vs relational, block vs object storage) to optimize performance.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Mechanical sympathy emphasizes aligning technology choices with specific workload access patterns.
optionExplanations.B: Stop guessing capacity is a general cloud advantage and Reliability design principle.
optionExplanations.C: Using serverless is a valid architectural pattern, but mechanical sympathy covers matching specific technologies to access patterns.
optionExplanations.D: Go global in minutes describes multi-region deployment capability.

keyConcept: Mechanical sympathy: understanding technology capabilities and selecting appropriate data/compute services for workload characteristics.

question: A company decides to move an on-premises virtual machine to an Amazon EC2 instance without modifying its core code or architecture ('lift and shift'). Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Rehosting (also known as 'lift and shift') involves moving applications from on-premises to the cloud without making architectural or code modifications.

optionExplanations.A: Replatforming involves making minor cloud optimizations (like switching to managed database) without changing code.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Rehost is moving systems as-is directly onto cloud VMs (EC2).
optionExplanations.C: Refactoring involves redesigning the application using cloud-native architectures (serverless, microservices).
optionExplanations.D: Repurchasing involves dropping the existing product and moving to a SaaS solution.

keyConcept: Rehosting ('Lift and Shift'): migrating applications to AWS without code or architecture modifications.

question: An organization migrates its self-hosted on-premises Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle to eliminate database administrative tasks without altering application database queries. Which migration strategy does this represent?
explanation: Replatforming (also known as 'lift, tinker, and shift') involves making targeted cloud optimizations—such as moving from self-managed database servers to a managed service like Amazon RDS—without altering the core application architecture.

optionExplanations.A: Rehosting would mean running Oracle inside a self-managed EC2 instance without changing management model.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Replatforming adopts cloud-managed equivalents without rewriting the core application.
optionExplanations.C: Retiring means decommissioning applications that are no longer needed.
optionExplanations.D: Retaining means keeping applications in the on-premises environment.

keyConcept: Replatforming ('Lift, Tinker, and Shift'): swapping infrastructure components for managed services without rewriting code.

question: An enterprise rewrites a monolithic on-premises application into serverless microservices using AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB to achieve extreme elasticity and agility. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Refactoring (or re-architecting) involves reimagining how an application is architected and developed using cloud-native features such as microservices, serverless, and containerization.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Refactoring redesigns the application from the ground up to take full advantage of cloud-native capabilities.
optionExplanations.B: Rehosting is moving as-is without code changes.
optionExplanations.C: Repurchasing is purchasing an off-the-shelf SaaS package.
optionExplanations.D: Retaining is keeping the system on-premises.

keyConcept: Refactoring / Re-architecting: rebuilding an application using cloud-native architectures like serverless and microservices.

question: A company decides to replace its legacy on-premises customer relationship management (CRM) software with a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform purchased through AWS Marketplace. Which migration strategy describes this?
explanation: Repurchasing (often called 'drop and shop') involves moving to a different product, typically a SaaS solution, and abandoning the legacy customized application.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Repurchasing substitutes a custom or legacy system with a commercial SaaS product.
optionExplanations.B: Rehosting moves the existing application to the cloud as-is.
optionExplanations.C: Replatforming moves to a managed cloud database or container runtime without changing software.
optionExplanations.D: Retiring decommissions applications without replacing them.

keyConcept: Repurchasing ('Drop and Shop'): switching from a legacy custom system to a SaaS subscription model.

question: During an application portfolio discovery assessment, an IT team discovers that 15% of servers host outdated reporting tools that nobody in the business accesses. Which migration strategy should they apply to these servers?
explanation: Retiring involves identifying applications and hardware that are no longer useful to the business and safely shutting them down, freeing budget and operational focus.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Decommissioning unused systems reduces migration scope and cuts operational cost.
optionExplanations.B: Rehosting unused systems incurs unnecessary cloud spend.
optionExplanations.C: Refactoring requires high development effort and should not be spent on unused systems.
optionExplanations.D: Replatforming unused systems wastes engineering effort.

keyConcept: Retire: decommissioning and turning off applications that are no longer useful to the organization.

question: A company has a legacy mainframe application that cannot be easily migrated to the cloud due to hardware dependencies, but needs to keep running in the on-premises data center for the next two years. Which migration strategy applies?
explanation: Retaining involves leaving applications in their current on-premises environment because of migration complexity, compliance requirements, or lack of business justification to migrate immediately.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Retaining defers migration and keeps legacy applications on-premises.
optionExplanations.B: Repurchasing replaces the software with a SaaS alternative.
optionExplanations.C: Rehosting moves the workload to cloud virtual machines.
optionExplanations.D: Retiring decommissions the application completely.

keyConcept: Retain: keeping applications on-premises when migration is not currently feasible or justified.

question: Which TWO cloud migration strategies are recognized within the AWS 7 Rs migration framework? (Select TWO.)
explanation: The AWS 7 Rs migration strategies are: Rehost (lift and shift), Relocate, Replatform (lift, tinker, and shift), Refactor/Rearchitect, Repurchase (drop and shop), Retain, and Retire.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Rehost moves applications to AWS without making architecture changes.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Replatform makes targeted cloud optimizations (e.g., moving to Amazon RDS) without changing the core application code.
optionExplanations.C: Recalibrate is not one of the AWS 7 Rs migration strategies.
optionExplanations.D: Restructure is not one of the AWS 7 Rs migration strategies (the correct term is Refactor/Rearchitect).
optionExplanations.E: Rebalance is not one of the AWS 7 Rs migration strategies.

keyConcept: The AWS 7 Rs migration strategies include Rehost, Relocate, Replatform, Refactor, Repurchase, Retain, and Retire.

question: Which perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) focuses on training, organizational structure, skills gap analysis, and preparing the workforce for cloud transformation?
explanation: The People perspective of AWS CAF focuses on cultural change, staff training, cloud readiness, leadership, and evolving organizational roles.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The People perspective evaluates human capital, training, and team readiness.
optionExplanations.B: The Platform perspective focuses on data architectures, landing zones, and cloud infrastructure.
optionExplanations.C: The Security perspective focuses on data protection, compliance, and identity.
optionExplanations.D: The Operations perspective focuses on service management and operational health.

keyConcept: AWS CAF People Perspective: bridges the skills gap and guides staff readiness and culture during cloud adoption.

question: Which service helps businesses accelerate migrations by automatically capturing on-premises server specifications, running processes, and network dependencies before cloud migration?
explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects data about on-premises data centers (server performance, configuration data, and running processes) to help plan cloud migration projects.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Application Discovery Service maps on-premises infrastructure dependencies to plan migration waves.
optionExplanations.B: AWS CodeBuild is a continuous integration service that compiles source code and runs tests.
optionExplanations.C: AWS CloudHSM is a dedicated hardware security module for cryptography.
optionExplanations.D: Amazon Inspector scans cloud compute resources for vulnerabilities, not discovering on-premises assets.

keyConcept: AWS Application Discovery Service: discovers and maps on-premises servers, dependencies, and performance data for migration planning.

question: A company wants to calculate the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for running workloads in AWS versus on-premises. Which expense is an on-premises cost that is eliminated or significantly reduced in the AWS Cloud?

options.text: Data center power, cooling, and physical building maintenance

explanation: In an on-premises data center, organizations must fund facility construction, electricity, cooling, physical security, and rack hardware maintenance. AWS manages this infrastructure, eliminating these costs.

optionExplanations.A: Application software engineering and business logic development costs exist regardless of deployment model.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Facilities, electricity, HVAC, and physical data center upkeep are eliminated for cloud customers.
optionExplanations.C: There are no database user account creation fees in AWS.
optionExplanations.D: Support engineers are still needed to maintain application features.

keyConcept: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): cloud removes physical facility costs including power, cooling, floor space, and hardware maintenance.

question: What does the cloud economics practice of 'rightsizing' Amazon EC2 instances refer to?

options.text: Purchasing the largest available instance type to prepare for future growth
Matching instance types and sizes to workload performance requirements at the lowest cost
Replacing software licenses with hardware leases
Locking all virtual machines into three-year non-cancelable contracts

explanation: Rightsizing is the process of reviewing running resources and resizing or terminating them to match workload requirements at the lowest possible cost.

optionExplanations.A: Over-provisioning large instances is the opposite of rightsizing and wastes money.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Rightsizing matches compute, memory, and storage to actual workload requirements.
optionExplanations.C: Cloud economics replaces hardware leasing with variable pay-as-you-go pricing.
optionExplanations.D: Commitments should be applied after rightsizing has eliminated idle capacity.

keyConcept: Rightsizing: optimizing instance types and sizes based on real utilization metrics to minimize waste.

question: A company already owns software licenses for Microsoft Windows Server and SQL Server with Software Assurance and wants to run them on dedicated hardware in AWS. Which licensing option supports this?

options.text: Bring Your Own License (BYOL) on Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts

explanation: Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts allow customers to Bring Your Own License (BYOL) for eligible software licensed on per-socket, per-core, or per-VM bases.

optionExplanations.A: License-Included provides licenses directly billed through AWS.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. EC2 Dedicated Hosts satisfy compliance and licensing terms for BYOL software.
optionExplanations.C: Spot subscriptions are for interruptible compute capacity.
optionExplanations.D: AWS Free Tier provides trial usage, not enterprise BYOL hosting.

keyConcept: Bring Your Own License (BYOL): running existing customer-owned software licenses on Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts.

question: Which of the following is considered a capital expenditure (CapEx) in a traditional IT environment rather than an operational expenditure (OpEx)?

options.text: Purchasing physical network routers and enterprise storage SAN arrays
Paying monthly AWS CloudWatch metrics charges
Paying hourly on-demand EC2 instance compute costs
Paying monthly AWS Support subscription fees

explanation: Capital expenditures (CapEx) are upfront investments in physical property, plant, and hardware equipment that are depreciated over multiple years. In contrast, cloud usage is billed as operational expenses (OpEx).

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Buying storage arrays and network hardware requires heavy upfront capital investment.
optionExplanations.B: Monthly CloudWatch fees are operational variable expenses.
optionExplanations.C: Hourly on-demand EC2 costs are operational variable expenses.
optionExplanations.D: AWS Support fees are monthly operational expenses.

keyConcept: CapEx vs OpEx: physical servers/SANs are upfront capital investments; cloud services are pay-as-you-go operational expenses.

question: A company experiences lower unit costs on AWS compute and storage services over time because AWS continuously passes along the financial savings of operating at massive scale. Which cloud economics benefit does this demonstrate?
explanation: Because usage from hundreds of thousands of customers is aggregated in the cloud, AWS achieves higher economies of scale, translating into lower pay-as-you-go prices and frequent price reductions.

optionExplanations.A: The cloud replaces upfront capital expense (CapEx) with low variable operational expense (OpEx).
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Economies of scale allow AWS to pass cost savings back to customers through price drops.
optionExplanations.C: Customers still share security responsibilities under the shared responsibility model.
optionExplanations.D: Economies of scale result from multi-tenant efficiencies, not dedicated host isolation.

keyConcept: Benefit from massive economies of scale: AWS aggregates usage to achieve lower unit costs and pass savings to customers.

question: Why does automating infrastructure deployments with infrastructure as code (IaC) lead to reduced operational costs?

options.text: It grants unlimited free compute capacity
It reduces manual configuration errors and administrative effort while enabling automated teardown of idle resources
It eliminates all software licensing requirements
It forces all resources to run in the lowest-cost AWS Region

explanation: Automation through infrastructure as code (like AWS CloudFormation) reduces repetitive manual tasks, prevents costly misconfigurations, and makes it trivial to destroy non-production environments when not in use.

optionExplanations.A: IaC does not make AWS compute free.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Automation decreases engineering overhead, accelerates time to market, and prevents wasteful idle resources.
optionExplanations.C: Software licenses still apply to automated infrastructure.
optionExplanations.D: IaC templates deploy to the Region configured by the administrator.

keyConcept: Automation Economics: lowers labor costs, eliminates human configuration error, and enables scheduled teardown of idle environments.

question: How does the AWS consumption-based pricing model help organizations improve return on investment (ROI)?

options.text: Customers pay only for active resources consumed, eliminating capital tied up in idle capacity
Hardware ownership passes to the customer after 12 consecutive months of use
All data transfer fees are permanently waived after reaching gold support status
AWS covers all third-party software licensing fees

explanation: Pay-as-you-go pricing aligns costs directly with business demand. When demand drops, resources scale down and costs drop, maximizing capital efficiency and ROI.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Paying only for what is consumed prevents waste from idle, over-provisioned infrastructure.
optionExplanations.B: AWS retains ownership and maintenance of all cloud hardware.
optionExplanations.C: Data transfer fees follow standard published pricing.
optionExplanations.D: Third-party software fees are the customer's responsibility.

keyConcept: Pay-as-you-go: variable consumption pricing aligns infrastructure expenditure directly with business demand.

question: An organization moves development and QA environments to AWS and configures automated scripts to shut them down outside business hours (nights and weekends). How does this benefit cloud economics?

options.text: It reduces compute costs by approximately 70% compared to running servers 24/7
It doubles the storage volume capacity at no cost
It automatically upgrades instance types to the latest generation
It transfers OS patching responsibility to AWS

explanation: Because cloud compute is billed per second/hour, stopping instances during non-working hours (128 out of 168 hours in a week) saves up to ~70% on compute spending compared to running them 24/7.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Stopping non-production servers during nights and weekends substantially reduces compute charges.
optionExplanations.B: Storage capacity is not modified or doubled by stopping instances.
optionExplanations.C: Instance generations are chosen by the administrator, not automatically upgraded.
optionExplanations.D: Instance management remains under customer responsibility for Amazon EC2.

keyConcept: Scheduling non-production workloads: stopping idle servers during nights and weekends saves up to 70% on compute costs.

question: Which term describes the reduction in unit cost that AWS achieves through purchasing large volumes of IT equipment and running operations at global scale?
explanation: Economies of scale refers to the cost advantages that enterprises obtain due to their scale of operation, with cost per unit of output decreasing with increasing scale. AWS passes these savings to customers as price reductions.

optionExplanations.A: Horizontal scaling is adding more instances to handle load.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. High volume operations lower per-unit infrastructure costs.
optionExplanations.C: High availability is designing systems to operate without downtime.
optionExplanations.D: Elastic load balancing distributes incoming application traffic.

keyConcept: Economies of scale: purchasing and operating at immense global volume lowers per-unit hardware and power costs.
